title: Chrome ServiceWorker use-after-free can execute code outside the sandbox
summary: The ServiceWorker flaw permits code execution outside the sandbox through crafted HTML. Separate CSS, Layout and Accessibility use-after-free flaws permit execution inside the sandbox.

severity.rationale: A crafted page can execute code outside the sandbox without an additional configuration prerequisite in the vendor record. Unattended agent browsers need the fix within 24 hours.

affected.note: Stable: 157.0.8103.78/.79 on Windows and macOS; 157.0.8103.78 on Linux.
Windows and macOS. The release lists all four CVEs.

exposure: Browsers processing attacker-controlled HTML are exposed, including sandboxed agent browsers. Test-only browsers restricted to trusted application content have lower exposure.

params.instructions: Read the browser executable version and its release channel. Stable needs 157.0.8103.78 or later; Windows/macOS Extended Stable needs 156.0.8078.100 or later. Do not compare Extended Stable against the Stable threshold.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Update to the patched build for the installed release channel and restart browser processes.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updating and restarting can interrupt dependent workflows.

verification: Confirm the installed version and the component used by running processes meet the documented fix or containment condition.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
